note: Set A binds each ∂P/∂θ value to the aerodynamic power sensitivity to blade-pitch angle with the full row conditions (wind speed, rotor speed, pitch angle) and quotes that support them, and all three values match the table exactly. Set B reads the numbers correctly but attributes every column to the "Baseline Blade-Pitch Controller", so the ∂P/∂θ values are bound to the wrong property owner, and it pads the set with five bare wind-speed rows and four repeats of the constant rotor speed 12.1 rpm. B also drops rotor speed and pitch angle from the ∂P/∂θ conditions, which A keeps. Neither set captures the ∂P/∂θ values for rows 13.0, 14.0, 18.0 and 19.0, so A covers essentially the same engineering facts as B without the noise.
remarks: The table's subject is ∂P/∂θ (watt/rad) as a function of wind speed, rotor speed and pitch angle; the section heading (7.3 Baseline Blade-Pitch Controller) is context, but using it as the owning entity for every column loses the property ownership and turns row variables into pseudo-properties. Both sets leave out the ∂P/∂θ rows for 13.0 (6.60, -51.66E+6), 14.0 (8.70, -58.44E+6), 18.0 (14.92, -83.94E+6) and 19.0 (16.23, -90.67E+6); B's bare "Wind Speed = 14.0/18.0 m/s" claims do not capture those facts. B's repeated "Rotor Speed = 12.1 rpm" claims are one constant table column restated per row. Set B's quotes use ellipses between header and value; the values are still supported, but full-row quotes (as in A) are more verifiable.
